briefing.opening: Welcome. I will now begin the climate briefing for October 4, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Intensifying Climate Crisis: A Global Warning
sections.content: Today's news warns of an intensifying global climate crisis. Domestically, academic attention is focused on the collapse of Antarctic glaciers, with discussions even mentioning a 'Doomsday for Earth' scenario [1]. Internationally, a massive loss of ice has been reported, including approximately 20% of Swiss glaciers disappearing in 2026, which has alarmed scientists [22]. New studies are revealing an increasingly strengthened link between global warming and extreme weather events [24], and past instances, such as Australia's 'Millennium Drought' from 1997 to 2009, serve as a reminder of the severity of these extreme climate phenomena [2]. Furthermore, direct impacts of climate change are being witnessed in various regions worldwide, including a late-season heatwave striking Southern California [37], and endangered fog oasis trees in Lima, Peru, facing a dual threat from climate change and unchecked urban growth [30].

sections.title: ⚖️ Climate Change and Legal Responsibility: Increasing Role of the Judiciary
sections.content: As damages from climate change increase, discussions on legal responsibility are becoming more active. Climate change-related cases are being addressed by the International Court of Justice [15], and the U.S. Supreme Court is set to hear major climate change lawsuits related to the devastating Marshall and Colorado wildfires [16, 23, 25, 28]. These hearings are expected to set important precedents for future climate change litigation [20]. Meanwhile, Mark Carney's statement that the economy takes precedence over climate change in relation to new pipeline construction [21], once again highlights the complex balancing act between climate action and economic development.

sections.title: 🌱 Domestic and International Climate Action and Adaptation Efforts
sections.content: Amidst this crisis, various domestic and international efforts to address climate change continue. Domestically, Cheonan City and Gwacheon City are holding promotional events for carbon neutrality practices and final reporting sessions for their local energy plans [3, 4, 9], while Seongnam City is encouraging citizen participation through a carbon neutrality idea contest [5]. Gwangju City has proposed a major industrial transformation utilizing renewable energy [7], and the development of technology linking volatile renewable energy with hydrogen production has also commenced [8]. Internationally, the potential for ancient African rice to aid farmers in coping with climate change has been suggested [19, 32], and mapping research identifying climate change survival zones for Himalayan medicinal plants is underway [26]. These are examples of active research and policies aimed at strengthening adaptation and resilience.

sections.title: 🔬 Scientific Understanding and Societal Discourse on Climate Change
sections.content: Scientific understanding of climate change is deepening, and the broader societal discourse is expanding. New research findings are being published, such as the phenomenon of the atmosphere slowing Earth's rotation being identified as a subtle signal of climate change [14]. Furthermore, review articles for the climate change satirical films 'A Statement' and 'Digger' have been reported [13, 18, 31], increasing public interest in how climate change is addressed in popular culture. Meanwhile, reports indicating rising prices for certain food items due to climate change [33], are raising awareness of the impact of climate change on the everyday economy.

briefing.closing: Today's briefing highlights the severity of the climate crisis and the multifaceted efforts being made globally to address it. Through continued attention and cooperation, we must overcome the challenges of climate change. This concludes today's climate briefing.

articles.description: Gangwon Province announced on the 4th that it will invest 147 billion KRW this year to implement disaster prevention projects and agricultural policy insurance support projects.
